To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the performance of any model on an unsupervised similarity task is directly linked to the quality of the optimal representation space, (b) shallow models can outperform deep models on unsupervised similarity if their representation spaces are optimal, and (c) the performance of deep models can be improved on unsupervised tasks by finding optimal representation spaces.

(i) a representation space that is well-suited for a particular similarity task is a function of the task and the input data; (ii) for many tasks, this optimal representation space is not the space induced by the model’s architecture, and (iii) the performance of a model can be improved by projecting the output vectors to a more suitable space, without any re-training
